contentBlocks.body: Reduce is not only for sums. By keeping the larger of the accumulator and the current item, you can fold a list down to its maximum. Seed the accumulator with the first element so the comparison starts from a real value.

contentBlocks.code:
const best = [3, 9, 2].reduce((max, value) => (value > max ? value : max));
// best is 9

contentBlocks.body: **Worked example.** The accumulator is the best candidate seen so far. Each comparison either replaces it with the current word or keeps it. The strict comparison keeps the earlier candidate on equal lengths.
Changing > to >= changes the tie rule. Tests should state whether the first or last tied item wins.

**Try a small change.** Add a second four-letter word and predict which one survives.

Then complete the independent check below without copying the example. Explain the boundary case in words before running it.
